entries.title: Psalms 94:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Utter - Or pour forth freely, constantly, abundantly, as a fountain doth waters (so this Hebrew word signifies.) Hard things - Insolent, and intolerable words against thee and thy people.

entries.title: Psalms 94:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Of Jacob - He who takes that name to himself, but has no regard to his people.

entries.title: Psalms 94:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Planted - The word is emphatical, signifying the excellent structure of the ear, or the several organs belonging to the sense of hearing. Formed - By which word he intimates the accurate and curious workmanship of the eye.

entries.title: Psalms 94:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Know - Mens thoughts and words and actions.

entries.title: Psalms 94:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thoughts - Yes, he knoweth all things, even the most secret things, as the thoughts of men; and in particular your thoughts; much more your practices.

entries.title: Psalms 94:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Blessed - Those afflictions which are accompanied with Divine instructions are great and true blessings.

entries.title: Psalms 94:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: But - God will declare himself to be a righteous judge, and will again establish justice in the earth. Follow - They will all approve of it, and imitate this justice of God in all their actions.

entries.title: Psalms 94:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rise - To defend and help me. I looked hither and thither, but none appeared; God alone helped me.

entries.title: Psalms 94:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Dwelt - In the place of silence, the grave.

entries.title: Psalms 94:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thoughts - While my heart was filled with various and perplexing thoughts, as this Hebrew word signifies. Comforts - Thy promises, and the remembrance of my former experience of thy care and kindness.

entries.title: Psalms 94:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shall - Wilt thou take part with the unrighteous powers of the world who oppress thy people. A law - By virtue of those unrighteous decrees which they have made.
